summary: An aggregate FILTER combined with an explicit window frame crashes target emission with an uncaught AttributeError on every route whose target is MySQL or SQL Server (8 of 42).
minimal_repro_sql: SELECT SUM(a) FILTER (WHERE b) OVER (ORDER BY d ROWS BETWEEN 1 PRECEDING AND CURRENT ROW) FROM t
contract_violated: Batch 31 requires target emission to raise on unsupported semantics and fail closed. An AttributeError escapes the diagnostic path entirely, so the caller gets a crash rather than a BLOCKED result with a diagnostic code.
traceback_tail: f"'{nulls_sort_change.strip()}' translation not supported in window function {window_this.sql_name()}"
why_the_synthetic_corpus_missed_it: corpus/development/queries.json contains COUNT(*) FILTER (WHERE status='OPEN') but never combines FILTER with OVER plus an explicit frame.

toolchain.note: two different pins of the same library in one repository

root_cause: Upstream sqlglot defect, reproduced in bare sqlglot at BOTH pins in this repository (30.13.0 used by sql-transpiler and 30.14.0 used by sql-dialect-engine): sqlglot/generator.py ordered_sql calls window_this.sql_name() on a Filter node while emitting a NULLS-ordering translation. Not an ELMOS logic error.
why_it_still_matters: Batch 31 requires target emission to raise on unsupported semantics and fail closed. This upstream crash is unguarded, so the caller gets an AttributeError instead of a BLOCKED TranspileResult with a diagnostic code. Bumping the pin does not fix it; the emission path needs to catch non-Unsupported exceptions and convert them into a fail-closed diagnostic.
